                            UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT                                  09/08/2026
                         FOR THE EASTERN DISTRICT OF VIRGINIA
                                 ALEXANDRIA DIVISION


  MARVELLE J. BALLENTINE,

                 Plaintiff,

                 v.                                           Case No. 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD
                                                              The Honorable Judge
                                                              Rossie D. Alston Jr.


  KATIE HALL, individually;
  NATIONAL CENTER FOR MISSING & EXPLOITED CHILDREN;
  META PLATFORMS, INC.;
  and JOHN/JANE DOES 1-6,

                 Defendants.


              PLAINTIFF'S MOTION FOR LEAVE TO FILE SECOND AMENDED
         AND SUPPLEMENTAL COMPLAINT PURSUANT TO FEDERAL RULES
                 OF CIVIL PROCEDURE 15(a)(2) AND 15(d), AND REQUEST
                      FOR EXPEDITED DETERMINATION ON THE PAPERS


         Plaintiff Marvelle J. Ballentine moves under Federal Rules of Civil Procedure 15(a)(2) and

  lS(d) for leave to file the complete Second Amended and Supplemental Complaint attached as

  Exhibit A. Plaintiff requests expedited determination of this Motion on the papers. The

  accompanying Memorandum in Support develops the grounds stated below, and Plaintiff

  incorporates it by reference.

         I.      THE COMPLETE PROPOSED PLEADING ELIMINATES THE FORM

                 OBJECTION RAISED IN ECF NO. 53

         1.      On September 3, 2026, Defendant Meta Platforms, Inc. ("Meta") filed its

  opposition to Plaintiff's pending Motion for Leave to File Supplemental Complaint Pursuant to

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD           Document 59        Filed 09/08/26      Page 2 of 10 PageID# 498




  Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 15(d) (ECF No. 26). ECF No. 53. Meta raises a form objection to

  ECF No. 26. Meta states that ECF No. 26 attached "only his supplemental allegations,

  'incorporating by reference' the remainder of his FAC," rather than "a copy of the proposed

  amended pleading in its entirety." ECF No. 53 at 3 n.1. Plaintiff does not concede that the objection

  was well taken. Plaintiff has instead elected to eliminate that procedural dispute rather than require

  the Court to adjudicate it. Exhibit A is one complete proposed Second Amended and Supplemental

  Complaint. It incorporates no prior pleading by reference. This Motion therefore places the entire

  proposed operative pleading before the Court in one document.

         II.     RELIEF REQUESTED

         2.      Plaintiff requests leave to file the proposed Second Amended and Supplemental

  Complaint ("SAC") attached as Exhibit A. Plaintiff further requests that the Court deem Exhibit A

  filed, and deem it the operative pleading in this action, upon entry of the order granting leave.

  Plaintiff further requests that, upon granting leave, the Court deny ECF No. 26 as moot and deny

  Plaintiff's Motion for Leave to File Sur-Reply (ECF No. 43) as moot.

         III.    THE PROPOSED PLEADING

         3.      The First Amended Complaint (ECF No. 5) is the operative pleading. The proposed

  SAC replaces the First Amended Complaint with one integrated pleading.

         4.      The proposed SAC adds no defendant. The proposed SAC adds no cause of action.

  The proposed SAC adds no category of relief. The proposed SAC retains the six-count structure of

  the First Amended Complaint. Count I and Count II plead defamation per se and defamation by

  implication against Defendants Katie Hall and the National Center for Missing & Exploited

  Children ("NCMEC"). Count III pleads intentional infliction of emotional distress against Hall and

  NCMEC. Count IV pleads conspiracy under the first clause of 42 U.S.C. § 1985(2) against all

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD           Document 59        Filed 09/08/26      Page 3 of 10 PageID# 499




  Defendants. Count V pleads Virginia common-law conspiracy against all Defendants. Count VI

  pleads insulting words under Va. Code§ 8.01-45 against Hall and NCMEC.

         5.      The proposed SAC pleads additional facts in four categories. First, the proposed

  SAC pleads facts concerning the source-level falsity of the asserted association between the two

  CyberTipline reports and "Marvelle J. Ballentine." The proposed SAC pleads facts concerning the

  person-level falsity of the implication that the reports concerned Plaintiff personally. The proposed

  SAC pleads facts concerning the defamatory implication arising from the letters' wording and

  omitted limitations. Ex. A§§ J, K, S. Second, the proposed SAC pleads facts concerning Plaintiff's

  legal name and Plaintiff's Meta account. Those facts include that Plaintiff never used "Marvelle J.

  Ballentine" to create, identify, or operate any Meta account. Ex. A § S; Ex. B ,, 2-10. Third, the

  proposed SAC pleads events occurring after the First Amended Complaint. Those events bear on

  Defendants' knowledge, on Defendants' state of mind, on the unresolved referent of the April 22,

  2026 letters, and on Plaintiff's continuing injury. Ex. A§ O; Ex. A, Count III. Fourth, the proposed

  SAC incorporates the post-filing allegations presently proposed through ECF No. 26. Those

  allegations include NCMEC's August 12, 2026 memorandum, the August 13, 2026

  communications with counsel for NCMEC and Hall, and Meta's August 13, 2026 filing in the

  Northern District of California. The SAC also pleads Hall's September 2, 2026 filings expressly

  adopting NCMEC's litigation positions. Ex. A§ O; Ex. A, Counts III, IV.

         6.      The    proposed    SAC     combines    amendment      under   Rule    15(a)(2)   with

  supplementation under Rule 15(d) in one pleading. The amended matter and the supplemental

  matter concern the same two April 22, 2026 letters, the same Defendants, and the same six claims.

         IV.     RELATIONSHIP TO ECF NOS. 26 AND 43

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD          Document 59        Filed 09/08/26       Page 4 of 10 PageID# 500




         7.     ECF No. 26 remains pending unless and until the Court grants this Motion. Upon

  grant of this Motion, the supplemental allegations proposed through ECF No. 26 become part of

  the operative pleading through the complete SAC, and ECF No. 26 becomes moot. If the Court

  denies this Motion, ECF No. 26 remains for decision on its own terms.

         8.     ECF No. 43 is Plaintiff's Motion for Leave to File Sur-Reply. ECF Nos. 43, 44.

  That motion is directed to Meta's Rule 12 briefing addressed to the First Amended Complaint. ECF

  Nos. 22, 39. Upon grant of this Motion, the SAC replaces the First Amended Complaint. Plaintiff

  then no longer requires the separate sur-reply vehicle, and ECF No. 43 becomes moot.

         9.     This Motion therefore permits one complete operative pleading to replace two

  separate pending procedural requests.

         V.     PROCEDURAL POSTURE

         10.    This action is at the pleading stage. Plaintiff filed the original Complaint on July 30,

  2026 (ECF No. 1). Plaintiff filed the First Amended Complaint on August 6, 2026 (ECF No. 5).

  NCMEC moved to dismiss the First Amended Complaint on August 12, 2026 (ECF Nos. 10, 11).

  Meta moved to dismiss the First Amended Complaint on August 21, 2026 (ECF Nos. 21, 22). Meta

  filed its reply on August 31, 2026 (ECF No. 39). On September 2, 2026, Hall moved to dismiss the

  First Amended Complaint and expressly adopted and joined NCMEC's Motion to Dismiss and

  Memorandum in Support (ECF No. 45). On September 2, 2026, the Court vacated the hearing on

  NCMEC's motion to dismiss and directed that the motion be decided on the papers (ECF No. 50).

         11.    Plaintiff filed ECF No. 26 on August 21, 2026 (ECF Nos. 26, 27, 28). NCMEC

  opposed ECF No. 26 on August 26, 2026 (ECF No. 32). Plaintiff replied the same day (ECF No.

  35). Hall opposed ECF No. 26 on September 2, 2026 (ECF No. 47). Meta opposed ECF No. 26 on

  September 3, 2026 (ECF No. 53). ECF No. 26 is set for hearing on September 25, 2026, at 10:00

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD          Document 59        Filed 09/08/26     Page 5 of 10 PageID# 501




  a.m., before Magistrate Judge Ivan D. Davis, together with Plaintiff's Rule 26(d)(l) motion (ECF

  No. 15). Plaintiff is contemporaneously filing a separate motion to vacate the September 25, 2026

  hearing as to ECF No. 26 only and to submit ECF No. 26 on the papers, without prejudice to ECF

  No.15.

           12.    On September 1, 2026, Plaintiff filed ECF No. 43, Plaintiff's Motion for Leave to

  File Sur-Reply, with a Memorandum in Support (ECF No. 44), directed to Meta's reply in support

  of its motion to dismiss the First Amended Complaint (ECF No. 39).

           13.    As of the filing of this Motion, no Defendant has answered. No scheduling order has

  issued under Rule 16(b). No conference has occurred under Rule 26(f). Merits discovery has not

  commenced.

           VI.    BRIEFING AND DETERMINATION ON THE PAPERS

           14.    This Motion is submitted under the ordinary briefing schedule of Local Civil Rule

  7(F)(l). Plaintiff waives oral argument on this Motion and is filing a Notice of Waiver of Oral

  Argument with it. Plaintiff requests expedited determination of this Motion on the papers upon

  completion of the briefing permitted by the Local Rules.

           VII.   RELIEF

           WHEREFORE, Plaintiff respectfully requests that the Court enter an order: (a) granting

  Plaintiff leave under Federal Rules of Civil Procedure 15(a)(2) and 15(d) to file the complete

  Second Amended and Supplemental Complaint attached as Exhibit A, deeming Exhibit A filed,

  and deeming it the operative pleading in this action; (b) upon granting leave, denying ECF No. 26

  as moot; (c) upon granting leave, denying ECF No. 43 as moot; (d) granting expedited

  determination of this Motion on the papers upon completion of briefing under Local Civil Rule

  7(F)(l); (e) directing the Clerk, to the extent administratively necessary, to docket the Second

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD         Document 59        Filed 09/08/26     Page 6 of 10 PageID# 502




  Amended and Supplemental Complaint separately as the operative complaint; and (f) providing

  that Defendants shall respond to the Second Amended and Supplemental Complaint within the

  time prescribed by the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure or such other time as the Court directs. A

  proposed order is submitted with this Motion.
